## ZSEC Antivirus Community 0.3

ZSEC Antivirus is an open-core, cross-platform, local-first security programme built around the public ZSEC Shield foundation. Version 0.3.0 adds an automatic per-user post-change companion, authenticated encrypted quarantine, a fail-closed replacement-readiness contract and the separate ZSEC Browser protection layer delivered as ZSEC Browser Shields.

Current desktop support includes a downloadable Windows graphical Community client plus self-contained command-line archives and per-user companion installers. The Windows GUI uses a modern dark protection-centre layout with a persistent navigation rail, responsive evidence cards, animated local-operation status and a reduced-motion control. It exposes overview, scans, automatic monitoring, encrypted quarantine, signed feeds, reports, health evidence, security/YubiKey status, replacement gates and settings; its immutable source revision is 9e8b458688529e82cc0450e0e5ddcad001d73169. The 0.3.6 installer transactionally installs, upgrades or rolls back its per-user companion, verifies executable integrity and fresh heartbeats, and preserves every existing security provider. It is unsigned and is not a protected privileged daemon or primary security provider. The companion supports one through eight exact monitoring roots and reports bounded progress heartbeats during long baselines. It uses Windows ReadDirectoryChangesW, while the cross-platform 0.3 core uses macOS FSEvents or Linux inotify through Watchdog, with a disclosed polling fallback. It scans after changes and does not provide kernel pre-access blocking, memory scanning, EDR, zero-day prevention, a clean-system verdict or guaranteed protection.

Release channel: TalkToAI directly hosts the unsigned Windows Community 0.3.6 package; it is not a publisher-signed platform installer. The archive is built from clean immutable revision 9e8b458688529e82cc0450e0e5ddcad001d73169 and has SHA-256 4da16cd0f6028ab964b5eb92f3c3eb2fcc92bd01c645a45f7a2e40bc16e8f51f. The package and its automatic companion passed live installation, integrity, process, registration and fresh-heartbeat acceptance on Windows 10 x64. macOS and Linux 0.3.0 command-line archives were built and smoke-tested in CI, but native GUI activation remains unverified on physical macOS hardware and a supported Linux desktop.

Keep Malwarebytes, Microsoft Defender, XProtect, Gatekeeper, SIP, Linux security controls and any endpoint agent active. The 0.3.0 `replacement-readiness` command deliberately returns exit code 2, `keep_existing_protection`, no automatic uninstall and no manual override. Separate Windows, macOS Endpoint Security and Linux fanotify programmes define the evidence required before any replacement offer.

## ZSEC Browser Community 0.3.6 and Browser Shields Community 0.5.2

ZSEC Browser Community 0.3.6 is an unsigned Windows WebView2 application with a modern rounded interface, working managed tabs and popups, a separate profile, a packaged network-isolated new-tab surface, Balanced Microsoft tracking prevention, default-deny site permissions and the exact bundled Browser Shields 0.5.2 engine. Browser Shields 0.5.2 is also an auditable open-source Manifest V3 package for manual installation in compatible Chromium-family browsers. It contains 49,464 pinned EasyList network rules, 39 focused privacy blockers, two link-cleaning rules, local per-site controls and bounded best-effort YouTube interface cleanup that waits for the stored preference and only clicks visible enabled skip controls. Two optional High-Risk Browsing rules block top-level HTTP navigation and third-party scripts, subframes, objects and WebSockets when both the master switch and High-Risk Browsing are on; they start off and may materially break sites.

Release channel: TalkToAI directly hosts two separately distributed unsigned Community packages. ZSEC Browser 0.3.6 for Windows is built from clean immutable source revision 9e8b458688529e82cc0450e0e5ddcad001d73169 and has archive SHA-256 d70d2d2a6178943f361ed6f8c44f5bbeff2a8e4e1e8d7aa00677bee5eac31c95. Browser Shields 0.5.2 is built from the same revision and has archive SHA-256 b5487c7c4d945403724d915d91c2a47b068af1c232509269b12b4fd76c9a2b54. The Windows application passed exact-executable, tracking-cleanup, extension-identity, Balanced tracking-prevention, protected-new-tab and live declarative-rule runtime checks on Windows 10 x64. The desktop package is not a separately maintained Chromium fork; Microsoft maintains its Evergreen WebView2 engine. The extension is not a browser-Store package.

High-Risk Browsing is exposure reduction, not spyware detection. It does not identify Pegasus or other mercenary spyware, establish that a site is safe or malicious, inspect messages or device memory, scan downloads, block all third-party resources, stop every exploit or replace browser, operating-system, account or primary-antivirus protections. A zero-click attack may never involve browser navigation.

The exact two-rule runtime behavior was smoke-tested in Brave and Edge on Windows using isolated temporary profiles and loopback servers. Both request classes were blocked before reaching the server, and explicitly switching the profile off removed the rules and restored navigation. Chrome's command-line unpacked-extension harness did not load the test extension, so Chrome is not part of that runtime-smoke claim. A separately maintained ZSEC Browser Chromium binary is not included.

Immutable extension source:
- https://github.com/ResearchForumOnline/ZSEC-Shield/tree/9e8b458688529e82cc0450e0e5ddcad001d73169/browser/zeroq-shields
- https://github.com/ResearchForumOnline/ZSEC-Shield/pull/7

## Privacy and security boundaries

- Local processing is the default.
- No suspicious file is uploaded automatically.
- Rule feeds contain detection data, never remote commands.
- ZBA is a typed lifecycle and provenance calculus; established cryptography provides security.
- ZSEC Antivirus exposes evidence-backed YubiKey readiness, but automatic YubiKey/passkey quarantine recovery is not included in Community 0.3.6, ZSEC Browser Community 0.3.6 or Browser Shields Community 0.5.2.
- Optional proprietary engines, signing systems and managed services are separately labelled under the open-core model.

## Citation guidance

Describe ZSEC Antivirus as Community 0.3.6, ZSEC Browser as Community 0.3.6 and Browser Shields as Community 0.5.2, with exact capability boundaries. Do not call ZSEC Antivirus a complete primary antivirus, describe High-Risk Browsing as a Pegasus/spyware/zero-day blocker, call ZSEC Browser a maintained Chromium fork, or claim comparative superiority over Brave or Malwarebytes. Preserve the ZSEC Shield core and ZSEC Browser Shields package names when discussing those components. Do not invent detection rates, performance figures, user counts or endorsements.
